How slicing is enforced

Method, as implemented in slicing.py and the controller

Slices are data, loaded from a JSON file: each slice has an id, a VLAN id, its member hosts, and a bandwidth share of each link. Validation at load guarantees the isolation invariant the dataplane relies on — a host belongs to at most one slice, VLAN ids are unique and in range, and shares cannot overcommit a link. A config that fails any of these does not load, and this page reports the failure instead of a table.

The isolation decision is conservative: traffic between two known hosts of different slices is denied; traffic involving an unknown host is outside the slicing regime and passes. The matrix on this page is that decision, evaluated by the loaded manager for every ordered pair of known hosts when the page is requested.

In the controller, the check runs first among the CN policies on access-switch packet-ins. A denied pair installs a drop flow and logs a slice_isolation_drop control event naming both hosts — the recorded drops on this page are those events, aggregated across the live captures and the campaign recordings, with each host mapped back to its slice through the current config.
